purpose: Agent-facing router for navigating MeTTa/TRM paper extensions and follow-on experiments.

routes.user_intent: Extend the current MeTTa/TRM paper with the cleanest next positive evidence.
routes.why: These projects keep the claim near the paper's strongest result: explicit symbolic gates expose verifier-visible state and improve small-model control-plane reliability.
routes.first_action: Create held-out rows and exact validators before adding model runs.
routes.paper_section: Main results extension or short addendum.
routes.overclaim_risk: Do not describe format or tool-contract wins as broad reasoning gains.

projects.title: Mixed Contract Compactification Suite
projects.first_artifact: A 50-row held-out mixed-contract dataset with explicit failure labels, exact validators, and near-miss cases.
projects.success_metric: Runtime+repair wins on exact contract validity without reducing semantic correctness on choice or summary rows.
projects.paper_claim: Small LLMs can act as proposal engines when explicit symbolic gates own observable output contracts.

projects.title: Real Tool-Contract Router
projects.first_artifact: A 30-60 row real-tool trace suite covering repo search, file lookup, shell-safe commands, calendar-like scheduling, weather-like queries, and JSON argument traps.
projects.success_metric: At least +0.20 absolute exact tool-call validity over baseline with zero schema-invalid commits on held-out tools.
projects.paper_claim: MeTTa/TRM improves control-plane tool-use reliability when tool schemas and arguments are verifier-visible.

routes.user_intent: Show whether the method transfers to hard logic and where it fails.
routes.why: Logic is the plausible hard positive target, but only if prompt-derived constraints, not answer signatures, drive projection.
routes.first_action: Write the leakage audit and proposal-tier labels before scoring improvements.
routes.overclaim_risk: Post-hoc projection can look strong while leaking target information; require a prompt-derived signature audit.

projects.title: Leakage-Safe Logic Signature Gate
projects.first_artifact: A tiny Campsite-style micro-suite with puzzle constraints, row/column signatures derivable from the prompt, and proposal-tier labels.
projects.success_metric: Improved cell accuracy and exactness over raw proposals, with an audit column proving no target answer signatures were imported.
projects.paper_claim: Symbolic amplification can help hard logic only after the model emits enough verifier-visible state.

projects.title: Live Symbolic Closure Threshold
projects.first_artifact: A proposal-tier classifier applied to local 3B logs across tool routing, contracts, ASCII tree, camp-gate, and math.
projects.success_metric: A clear threshold curve showing where the LLM becomes mostly a proposal generator and where it still needs scale.
projects.paper_claim: The compactification threshold is measurable as the amount of verifier-visible state emitted before symbolic execution takes over.

routes.user_intent: Make the paper more credible by showing where MeTTa/TRM does not replace scale.
routes.why: Hard math separates protocol/candidate-auditing gains from missing base-model solving competence.
routes.first_action: Build or import a teacher-candidate bank with numeric validators and error archetypes.
routes.overclaim_risk: Do not claim small-model math solving unless the model produced the correct candidate unaided.

projects.title: Math Teacher-Candidate Auditor
projects.first_artifact: A teacher-candidate bank with multiple proposed answers per item, numeric error archetypes, boxed-answer validators, and abstain labels.
projects.success_metric: Better candidate selection than keyword or always-first baselines while preserving a clear no-small-model-solve claim boundary.
projects.paper_claim: For hard math, MeTTa/TRM is useful as an auditor and protocol gate, not as a substitute solver.

routes.user_intent: Develop the psychometric/nuanced benchmark line rather than chase tiny scalar reward lifts.
routes.why: PsychoBench needs item-vector, subscale, and stability analysis; scalar reward alone hides the interesting effect.
routes.first_action: Run repeated probes and emit item vectors, subscale deltas, and stability bands.
routes.overclaim_risk: Variance reduction can be over-regularization if the gate collapses personality signal.

projects.title: PsychoBench Item-Vector Stability
projects.first_artifact: Repeated profile probes with item vectors, BFI subscale deltas, stability bands, and repair provenance.
projects.success_metric: Lower profile variance or clearer target-profile adherence without merely clipping every response to a safe midpoint.
projects.paper_claim: MeTTa/TRM can expose and control psychometric response geometry even when scalar reward barely moves.

routes.user_intent: Build reusable infrastructure for future skills and agents.
routes.why: MCP/tool lookup is a broad substrate where TRMs can optimize stable handles, call count, and token load.
routes.first_action: Define first-useful-hit, token-load, and call-count metrics before collecting traces.
routes.overclaim_risk: If the resource surface is tiny, direct scanning is the right baseline and TRM overhead is not justified.

projects.title: TRM-MCP Lookup Efficiency
projects.first_artifact: A benchmark over filesystem, GitHub, Postgres, and PrimeHub-schema MCP examples with call-count and token-load metrics.
projects.success_metric: Fewer calls and fewer loaded tokens before first useful answer at equal or better answer correctness.
projects.paper_claim: TRM rows can compactify tool/resource lookup when the target is stable handles rather than raw memorized answers.

projects.title: Real Tool-Contract Router
projects.first_artifact: A 30-60 row real-tool trace suite covering repo search, file lookup, shell-safe commands, calendar-like scheduling, weather-like queries, and JSON argument traps.
projects.success_metric: At least +0.20 absolute exact tool-call validity over baseline with zero schema-invalid commits on held-out tools.
projects.paper_claim: MeTTa/TRM improves control-plane tool-use reliability when tool schemas and arguments are verifier-visible.

routes.user_intent: Prepare for Snacksack or equivalent 9B/27B matched runs.
routes.why: The paper becomes stronger when the same row schema is run at 3B, 9B, and 27B with the same validators.
routes.first_action: Freeze row IDs, prompt construction, output schema, and validator code before changing models.
routes.overclaim_risk: Changing row selection or validators between scales makes the trend uninterpretable.

agent_loop.name: Classify the requested claim
agent_loop.output: Select one route_id and one primary project_id.
agent_loop.check: The selected project must have an evidence class that matches the requested paper claim.

agent_loop.name: Open the source spine
agent_loop.output: Read the project menu row, scale-transfer row, fork plan, and composition plan for the selected project.
agent_loop.check: Record source paths in the new study README so later agents can reproduce the reasoning.

agent_loop.name: Create a study folder
agent_loop.output: Use `research/studies/YYYY-MM-DD-<project_id>/` or a project subfolder under the active MeTTa study if it is clearly an extension.
agent_loop.check: Do not dump large model artifacts into Git unless they are small, interpretable result files.

agent_loop.name: Freeze rows and validators first
agent_loop.output: Emit row JSONL, validator code, and a row manifest before running models.
agent_loop.check: Rows must include split, env_family, expected observable state, and failure labels.

agent_loop.name: Run the smallest meaningful arms
agent_loop.output: Start with baseline, pure_trm, metta_runtime, and metta_runtime_repair unless the project defines a different matrix.
agent_loop.check: For local models, keep memory caps explicit and preserve prompt/output schemas for later 9B/27B runs.

agent_loop.name: Separate evidence classes
agent_loop.output: Mark each result as live model, deterministic replay, post-hoc projection, no-model verifier sweep, or control-plane simulation.
agent_loop.check: Never mix post-hoc projection with live benchmark columns.

agent_loop.name: Write the paper hook
agent_loop.output: Add a short findings.md with claim, limitation, metric table, and next run command.
agent_loop.check: Every positive claim must name the exact verifier-visible state that MeTTa/TRM controlled.

study_artifacts.purpose: One-page study index: route, project, source inputs, active claim, and artifact links.
Hypothesis, arms, validators, splits, stop rules, and paper claim boundary.
Frozen benchmark rows or proposal traces with stable IDs and split labels.
Exact validators or metric extractors used before model results are interpreted.
Prompt, model, memory, and arm configuration with enough detail for 9B/27B reruns.
Machine-readable result table with per-row arm scores and evidence_class.
Human-readable finding with metric table, failure breakdown, and paper-ready claim.
Explicit separation of live, deterministic, post-hoc, and control-plane evidence.
